accepted.evidence: Buddruss explicitly marks alák b- 'separate' as a loan from Hindi/Urdu alag. The first component is the attested Hindi alag 'separate' (CDIAL 700); the second is Buddruss's separate Shina b- 'become' head on the same page. Two ordered components preserve the light-verb construction rather than presenting the whole phrase as a single inherited stem.

Buddruss explicitly derives cilím 'water pipe' from Hindi/Persian čilam. Jambu's attested Hindi cilam 'receptacle part of hookah' (Strand) is the immediate documented Indo-Aryan donor; the Persian stage remains in the note, rather than skipping over the Hindi evidence.
